_doc:
The Civilization Expansion §6. A trade good is a THIRD thing: not an item you wear (player.bag), not a material you spend (craft.materials), but a product — made once, moved far, sold whole. It gets the fourth container and the fourth container is the only one in the game with a weight limit, because 'how much can this cart carry' is the question a trade run is made of.

THIS FILE IS INJECTED, NEVER MERGED INTO ANOTHER ONE. js/trade.js `installTradeGoods` copies each row into the live resources.materials map and pushes one recipe per good into the live refining.recipes array, at boot, in memory. data/resources.json is read by the scanner, the seam generator and the store-share caps, and twenty-two manufactured goods have no business in any of them; data/refining.json is the machine engine's file and it already queues, starves, unlocks-by-doing, slices and catches up, so a second recipe engine for trade goods would be a join nobody made. `kind: "trade"` is what keeps them out of the raw-share caps and out of a silo.

That is the same rule data/items.json taught: a shared data file is never edited in place.
_tagDoc: What a town wants or makes. EIGHT of them and no more, because a demand model with twenty axes is unreadable. js/trade.js works out a settlement's `needs` and `makes` from what it already is — its plots, its biome, its size, its culture and who holds the zone — so no settlement anywhere carries authored price data.
_weightDoc: `weight` is kilograms on the same scale data/resources.json already uses (iron ore 1.0, stone 1.6). `base` is gold at a town with no opinion either way; the real price is that times a multiplier between 0.55 and 1.85. `time` is seconds of machine at speed 1. Every input id below is a material the game actually produces — tests/tradegoods.test.js asserts it rather than trusting it.

goods.name: Sack of Charcoal
goods.desc: Twenty burnings' worth, bagged. Every forge in the world is somebody else's problem until it runs out of this.

goods.name: Block of Salt
goods.desc: Pressed and dried. Inland, this is the difference between meat and rot.

goods.name: Coil of Rope
goods.desc: Ten fathoms on a spindle. Nowhere has ever had enough.

goods.name: Keg of Nails
goods.desc: Four ingots drawn and cut. A town putting up roofs will take every keg you have.

goods.name: Pallet of Brick
goods.desc: Heavy, dull, and the most reliable money on any short road.

goods.name: Bundle of Beams
goods.desc: Eight squared beams, strapped. Somebody is raising a hall.

goods.name: Bolt of Cloth
goods.desc: Plain weave on a bolt. Light, valuable, and it does not spoil.

goods.name: Crate of Soap
goods.desc: Ash, fat and patience. A city will pay for it and a mining camp will pay more.

goods.name: Bale of Cured Hide
goods.desc: Six hides salted and rolled. Smells, travels well, always sells.

goods.name: Cask of Lamp Oil
goods.desc: A winter of evenings in one cask. The far north pays double and says thank you.

goods.name: Flask of Ink
goods.desc: Lampblack and gum. Two kilos of it is worth more than a wagon of stone.

goods.name: Crate of Pressed Rations
goods.desc: Twelve meals pressed flat and salted hard. What you sell to a place that has had a bad year.

goods.name: Coil of Wire
goods.desc: Drawn copper on a reel. Nothing modern happens anywhere without it.

goods.name: Crate of Glassware
goods.desc: Packed in straw and prayed over. Arrives intact more often than you would think.

goods.name: Bundle of Ingots
goods.desc: Ten ingots strapped with wire. Half the world's building starts as one of these.

goods.name: Tool Chest
goods.desc: Everything a working man owns, in one box. A new settlement buys these before it buys food.

goods.name: Case of Bearings
goods.desc: Ground true to a hair. Only a manufactory can hold the tolerance.

goods.name: Case of Silverware
goods.desc: Four pounds of silver beaten into things nobody needs. A city will not look at anything else.

goods.name: Keg of Blasting Powder
goods.desc: Do not drop it, do not let it get damp, and do not tell the guards what is in the wagon.

goods.name: Medicine Chest
goods.desc: Salves, tinctures and clean linen. The one cargo nobody robs twice.

goods.name: Set of Ground Lenses
goods.desc: Three lenses in a fitted case. Weeks of somebody's eyesight.

goods.name: Case of Control Boards
goods.desc: The most valuable thing a hand cart can carry, and it weighs less than a sack of charcoal.
